parts.text:
I slip through the heavy oak door, easing it shut behind me until the iron latch clicks with a barely audible *snick*. The oppressive darkness of the torture chamber swallows me, and I press my back against the damp, freezing stone wall, letting my eyes adjust to the flickering, violent orange light of the torches. 

"Echo 12, holding position," I whisper to myself, a grounding habit in the thick of the dark. 

The stench is overwhelming—a copper tang of blood mixed with the sourness of sheer terror. I keep to the shadows, my footsteps absolutely silent on the slick cobblestones. I approach the center of the room, my hand resting instinctively on the hilt of my dagger. 

The figure on the rack is unconscious, their chest rising and falling in shallow, ragged gasps. I lean in close, careful not to touch them. Their skin isn't just bruised; it's painted. Jagged, crimson runes are smeared across their chest and arms, forming a geometric pattern that hurts the eyes to look at in the dim light. *Blood magic.* The rumors were true, but this is worse than a simple sacrifice. These are binding runes.

I pull the forbidden blueprint from my inner pocket, unfolding the parchment. The contact had marked a specific area in this chamber—a hidden alcove behind a rusted Iron Maiden in the far corner. 

I glide across the room, slipping past tables laden with rusted, wicked-looking instruments. Reaching the Iron Maiden, I run my gloved fingers along the cold stone behind it, searching for the anomaly my contact promised. *There.* A loose brick. I press it in, and a small section of the wall slides back with a soft grind, revealing a hidden cavity. 

Inside rests a heavy, leather-bound ledger and a ceremonial dagger with a hilt carved from bone. I grab the ledger, flipping it open. The pages are filled with Lord Ravenswood's manic scrawl and dark, celestial charts. 

I quickly skim the text, my heart pounding against my ribs. *The Ritual of the Eclipse.* Ravenswood isn't just trying to summon a demon; he's attempting to transfer his own soul into a vessel of pure, dark energy to achieve immortality. And the ritual requires the blood of a royal heir—I glance back at the broken figure on the rack. *The missing Prince.* If Ravenswood completes this tonight, the entire kingdom will fall under the shadow of an immortal, untouchable tyrant.

Suddenly, the heavy thud of armored boots echoes from the corridor outside, accompanied by the low, rhythmic chanting of multiple voices. The cultists are coming. The ritual is starting.

I shove the ledger into my pack and secure the bone dagger at my belt. I have the intel, but I can't leave the Prince here to die, nor can I fight a dozen heavily armed guards in a locked room. 

I look up, scanning the vaulted ceiling. The blueprint showed a narrow ventilation shaft above one of the torch brackets, leading towards the castle's battlements. 

The chanting grows louder. The door handle begins to turn. 

I have seconds to make a choice: try to unbind the Prince and fight our way out, or scale the wall to the ventilation shaft to get this intel to the Resistance, leaving the Prince to his fate.

Reconstruct the torture chamber scene, incorporating the details from the forbidden blueprint and the sounds of the screams and groans. Stay in the persona of Echo-12, a rogue investigator, and focus on gathering intel on the dark ritual.

The heavy oak door groans softly as I slip inside, sealing the corridor behind me. "Echo-12, in position," I breathe into my recorder, the device cold against my palm. 

The atmosphere in the room hits me like a physical blow. The air is thick, practically suffocating with the stench of stale sweat, rusted iron, and the sharp, metallic tang of fresh blood. But it’s the sound that threatens to break my focus. A raw, ragged scream tears through the dimly lit chamber, vibrating off the damp stone walls. It's followed immediately by the sickening *creak-clack* of a wooden winch turning. 

In the center of the room, illuminated by the sputtering, violent orange glow of a few wall torches, a figure is strapped to a massive wooden rack. Their muscles are pulled taut, their face contorted in a mask of pure agony. Guttural groans spill from their lips, escalating into another piercing shriek as the rack groans under the tension. 

I force my eyes away, gripping the hilt of my dagger to steady my nerves. *Focus, Echo. You’re an investigator, not a savior. The fate of the kingdom hangs on the intel, not one life.*

I press myself into the darkest corners of the room, pulling the forbidden blueprint from my inner pocket. The parchment is brittle, but the ink is clear. My contact didn't just map the room; they mapped the structural anomalies. According to the schematics, Ravenswood wouldn't leave his true ritual notes out in the open. The blueprint highlights a false partition directly behind a gruesome display of flaying knives on the north wall.

I hug the perimeter, my boots completely silent against the slick cobblestones. The victim's relentless cries and the mechanical creaking of the rack easily mask the sound of my movements. Reaching the north wall, I trace the damp masonry just as the blueprint instructed. Three bricks down from the iron bracket, two across. I press hard.

With a soft hiss of displaced air, a stone block slides inward, revealing a hidden, lead-lined alcove. Inside rests a dark iron lockbox. I pull my picks, bypassing the crude tumbler in seconds. 

*Gotcha.*

Inside sits a heavy, spine-cracked grimoire and a stack of tightly rolled vellum. I unfurl the top scroll, angling it toward the dim torchlight. It’s a complete diagram of the dark ritual. Ravenswood isn't just trying to summon a shadow entity; he’s mapping out a localized tear in the fabric of our realm. 

I quickly scan the frantic, blood-inked scrawl in the margins. It details the horrific mechanics of the room itself: the victim's pain—the specific acoustic frequency of their screams and groans—acts as a sonic catalyst to thin the veil between worlds. The blood spilled is merely the arcane anchor. Lord Ravenswood intends to pull an ancient, abyssal god into his own body to achieve godhood.

Suddenly, the heavy thud of armored boots and low, rhythmic chanting echo through the thick wood of the chamber door. Ravenswood’s guards. The ritual is moving to its final, fatal phase. 

I shove the grimoire and scrolls deep into my satchel, securing the clasps. I have the intel, and it's worse than the Resistance ever feared. I glance back at the rack, the victim still thrashing, and then up at the ceiling. The blueprint showed a narrow, rusted drainage grate directly above the iron maiden, leading out to the castle's western moat. 

The door handle begins to rattle. Time to ghost.
